mods.name: JEI for Horizon
mods.summary: An item and recipe viewer for Horizon: every item beside container screens, with search, recipes, uses, tooltips and bookmarks
mods.description:
An item and recipe viewer for Horizon (https://playhorizon.dev), the Rust reimplementation of Minecraft: Java Edition.

Horizon JEI is inspired by JustEnoughItems (JEI) (https://github.com/mezz/JustEnoughItems). JEI serves as the reference specification, while this project is a completely new Rust implementation built around Horizon's native hook points.

Version 0.2.1 — Overlay and bookmarks

Features
• Recipe Navigation: Browse recipe history with Back and click recipe slots to open the corresponding item.
• Recipe Placement: Use the + button to place a recipe into the open crafting grid, provided it is available in the recipe book.
• Item Giving: Give items through Options → Mods → JEI or /jei give. In creative mode, left-click gives one item and right-click gives a full stack. In survival mode, clicking opens the recipe viewer instead.
• Item Tooltips: Every tooltip the game shows, the panel's included, names the keys and counts exactly: R: Recipes (12), U: Uses (3), and a star on the stacks in your bar.
• Subtypes: Every (item, components) pair the recipe tables name is an item of its own in the list, so the potions and the tipped arrows are there like JEI's subtypes.
• Bookmarks: Press A over a stack to bookmark it. The bar sits at the screen's top left corner in two columns of twelve: the left button opens a bookmark's recipes, the right one its uses, shift-click or the middle button removes it, and dragging moves it. It is kept in config/jei/bookmarks.txt and returns with the next world.
• List Order & Config: By name or by id, from the settings page or /jei sort name|id, kept in config/jei/jei.cfg along with the tooltip hints and the bar.
• World Transition Fix: Session cache is properly invalidated on world transitions even when JEI is temporarily disabled, preventing stale item IDs or recipes from lingering across worlds.
• Localization: English and Spanish interface translations. Item names are retrieved directly from the game and respect the player's language.
• Diagnostics: /jei reports the game's recipe table sizes, /jei bookmarks clear empties the bar and /jei config says where its files are.

Current Limitations

Container slot click integration (R and U work over any slot, a click does not), the creative inventory panel, the non-recipe categories (anvil, grindstone, composter, and fuel), shift-click recipe placement, recipe transfer into furnaces, and the $tooltip / %creative tab searches are not yet supported.

Some of these features require native hook points that Horizon does not currently expose. See the JEI parity matrix (https://github.com/enderliker/horizon-jei/blob/main/docs/jei-parity.md) for implementation details.

Requirements & Security

Requires Horizon 26.3 and hook points version 313 or later: tested and verified on Horizon Nightly (6560641 and latest fdc87ae).

Horizon native mods are compiled directly into the game and are not sandboxed. Only build source code you trust.

Horizon JEI reads the game's items and recipes, its container interface, chat, tooltips and screens. It writes only its own folder, config/jei/ (jei.cfg for the options, bookmarks.txt for the bar), and nothing else. It makes no network connections.

*Unofficial project. Not affiliated with mezz, Mojang, Microsoft, or the Horizon project.*

mods.description:
An unofficial port of Jade (https://github.com/Snownee/Jade) 26.3.5 by Snownee to Horizon: the look-at overlay for blocks and entities, with its providers, themes, config screens, drag-to-place screen, profiles, keys, the /jade and /jadec commands and the jade:max_position_deviation game rule.

Rewritten in Rust for Horizon's hooks, so no original code runs. Not made or endorsed by Snownee, so please report problems to this project, not to them.

Missing or not the same:
• Java plugins for Jade can't run. Other mods register with this port's own provider functions.
• The icon style of the energy line shows redstone dust, because Jade's energy sprite isn't in Horizon's atlas.
• The game rule works through mixins on tables compiled into the game, so it is the part most likely to break on a Horizon update.

Tested on Windows, in single player, on LAN with one guest, and on a dedicated server with one client. Other platforms and Jade's mouse binds were not tested.

mods.description:

Mountain ranges, terrain density recipes, underground rivers and configurable terrain for Horizon 26.3. Source-only native mod: install in the launcher, then Build; runs with the game's account permissions. No Minecraft code or assets are included.

Enable under Options > Mods before opening a world. The mod's Settings page edits terrain and biome configuration. Config: config/tectonic-horizon.json in the game home. Invalid configuration logs a diagnostic and uses defaults. Restart after editing; new chunks only. Select increased height before world creation.

Pins upstream Horizon 8dbbde43501924d16497d251e6e9d08f812eafcd and Mixins e8cd0aa38cffef49cb2e088ef716baa107148c02. See docs/REVIEW-0.3.4.md for current validation and docs/VALIDATION.md for historical checks with their original revisions.

No block-for-block Java parity claim. Native river-decoration placement differs from Lithostitched. Java config UI and Terralith/CliffTree overlays are omitted. Other biome mods need their own Horizon ports.

Author-supplied screenshot captured November 1 in our Horizon fork; illustrative, not evidence of current upstream validation. Minimap is a separate mod. Original Tectonic by Apollo; Horizon adaptation by eltanschauung with Codex assistance. Source licenses, notices and provenance hashes retained.

mods.description:
An unofficial, experimental Rust port of Create (https://github.com/Creators-of-Create/Create), made by Delete228. It is not made or endorsed by the Create team; their original code is MIT and is credited in the mod's NOTICE.
• Drive machines with water wheels, hand cranks or a Creative Motor.
• Route power through shafts, gears, gearboxes, clutches and encased chain drives.
• Move items on basic belts and depots. Press sheets, mill ingredients, mix in a Basin or process items with a fan.

Install it as a native mod in Horizon Launcher and build the instance. It uses simple built-in models and standard Minecraft textures out of the box.

The original models and textures require the original Create 6.0.10 JAR for Minecraft 1.21.1 (NeoForge). Place one copy in the instance's horizon-mods/create-resources/ folder and restart Horizon. The JAR is optional and resources are imported locally. Supported JAR (https://modrinth.com/mod/create/version/UjX6dr61)

Moving contraptions, trains and Ponder are planned. Setup and compatibility (https://github.com/Delete228/create-horizon)

mods.name: Applied Energistics 2
mods.summary: Unofficial port of Applied Energistics 2 15.4.12: ME networks, autocrafting, spatial storage and more.
mods.description:
An unofficial port of Applied Energistics 2 15.4.12 to Horizon, not made or endorsed by its authors. Please report problems to this port, not to them.

Rewritten in Rust: ME networks, storage cells, autocrafting, the cable bus with facades, P2P tunnels, spatial storage, the guide and the Fluix Researcher.

One file, no separate content mod.

Optional integrations
Each is compiled in only when its mod is in the same build, so adding or removing JEI or Jade takes effect at the next build.
• With JEI: AE2's recipes and information pages, "+" transfer into terminals, and dragging items onto config slots.
• With Jade: network state, channels, P2P links, charge, crafting and stored power.

Missing or not the same
• No spatial dimension. Horizon mods can't add one. A player in a spatial cell goes to a walled plot far out in the End, so /tp and F3 say minecraft:the_end. A swap with a player takes up to about a second.
• No Java addons. AE2's Java API isn't available, and the integrations work only with the Horizon ports of JEI and Jade.
• Two storage buses on one inventory: only the first reaches it.
• Moving items costs power through terminals, interfaces, export buses and wireless terminals. An IO port and the crafting terminal's refills pay nothing yet.
• Power is judged once a second, so a network with too little goes down at the next look and comes back after about 40 ticks, where AE2's is at once and 32.
• Unformed crafting, quantum and spatial blocks join a network before they're formed.
• Autocrafting gaps: a pattern input of more than one is a single template, so some plans report items missing that AE2 would find. Blocking mode looks at all six sides, provider priority is ignored, and a machine's request for more than it can make crafts nothing.
• Other differences: machines have 6 or 4 orientations rather than 24, menus are in English, fluix tools are diamond tools, and guide scenes have no annotations.
• Crafting ETA is an estimate: 1.1% off on average on the test rig, 2.0% at worst.
• Nested P2P error is an approximation.
• World height: parts on cables assume -64 to 319.

The Fluix Researcher and its trades rely on mixins, so they are the part most likely to break on a Horizon update.

Tested
Tested on Horizon commit 6475f62, on Windows, in single player, on LAN with one guest, and on a dedicated server with one client, including attacks by a non-operator with a modified client. This version is built for Horizon commit 66f3981, where AE2 alone compiles but hasn't been run, and the JEI and Jade integrations haven't been compiled. Other platforms, more than one guest, pipes from other mods and speed against the Java mod were not tested.

Known issue
In some test runs, placing a part into a cable cell did nothing. It isn't one specific part, and it's probably lost test clicks, but that isn't proven.

Textures and models are CC BY-NC-SA 3.0: noncommercial use only.

mods.name: Silent's Gems
mods.summary: 21 gems with storage blocks and 84 ores, plus overworld, nether and end worldgen.
mods.description:
A port of Silent's Gems (https://github.com/SilentChaos512/SilentGems) by SilentChaos512
for Horizon: 21 gems, their storage blocks and their ores.

Implemented so far:
• The 21 gems as items (ruby, carnelian, topaz, citrine, heliodor, moldavite, peridot,
  turquoise, kyanite, sapphire, iolite, alexandrite, ammolite, rose quartz, garnet,
  aquamarine, tanzanite, opal, pearl, black diamond and white diamond) with their own
  textures and rarities.
• Their 21 storage blocks and 42 compression/decompression recipes, with 105 loot tables
  and the mod's own textures, models and language file.
• 84 ore blocks — overworld stone, deepslate, nether and end variants of every gem —
  with their block/item tags.
• Ore worldgen: the mod's own overworld, nether and end ore features, placed features
  and biome modifiers (56 worldgen files).
• A creative tab listing the 126 items of this slice.

Not yet ported:
• Slices 1–2 only: glowrose and other plants, tool/armour sets, lamps, glass, bricks and
  tiles, teleporters, the silver/chaos material line, food and the Silent Gear
  integration are not registered yet.
• An ore always drops one gem: silk touch returns the gem rather than the ore block and
  fortune does not multiply (the pin has no match_tool/apply_bonus).
• Ore experience is the template's (lapis, 2–5), not upstream's fixed 1–5 provider.
• Gem names use per-gem keys (item.silentgems.ruby) rather than upstream's shared %s
  template.
• No tooltip shows a gem's colour or harvest tier.

A content/logic data carry: the 21-gem registry is a test-only Rust module (no injection). MIT — the original copyright and licence notices are kept in
the port repository (see LICENSE and LICENSE-NOTICE.md there). Pinned to
Horizon 1d63e0a and horizon-mixins 5a64af93.

mods.name: Atlas
mods.summary: A clone of Xaero's Minimap and World Map: a sharp minimap, a world map of everywhere you've been, and waypoints.
mods.description:
Atlas is meant to be a close copy of Xaero's Minimap and Xaero's World Map for Horizon: the same look, the same keys and the same settings. The minimap, the world map and the waypoints share one map of the world, kept on disk per world, server and dimension.
• Minimap: drawn at your screen's resolution, turns with you, with entity dots that fade with height. Hold Tab for mob faces, player faces and item icons.
• World map (M): drag and zoom. B makes a waypoint under the pointer.
• Map modes: Auto (the surface in the open, the cave around you under a roof), Cave and Layer.
• Waypoints (U, B, H): sets, filter, Share, Teleport for operators, deathpoints, temporary waypoints, and labels in the world.
• Overlays: chunk grid, light overlay, slime chunks (with /atlas seed).
• Settings (Y): pages of options with search; /atlas sets exact values.

What it does and doesn't do. Atlas reads the world your client already has and draws on your screen. It writes only its own folder, horizon-mods/.horizon-mod-data/atlas/ (settings, waypoints and maps). It opens no network connections. It sends something to the server only when you click Teleport (a /tp command, for operators) or Share (a chat message with the waypoint).

Atlas is its own code. It copies the look and features of Xaero's mods, but no code or art comes from them, and it isn't made or endorsed by Xaero. Built on Waypoints by Nirokx (MIT); the map columns follow Horizon's minimap (MIT).

Checked on Horizon Nightly 2026-11-05 (66f3981). It reads the game's world directly, so a much newer Nightly may need a new release. Turn off Horizon's own Minimap to avoid two maps.

shaders.name: Daybreak
shaders.summary: Sun shadows, reflective water, waving plants, coloured light, sun rays and bloom, built to cost as little GPU time as possible.
shaders.description:
Daybreak is a shader pack in Horizon's own format. It runs inside Horizon's renderer, so Horizon's culling, batching and LOD stay in charge, and it adds as little GPU time as it can.
• Sun and moon shadows with smooth edges
• Warm sunlight, blue sky light in the shade, a dim blue night
• Coloured block light: soul fire blue, redstone red, copper green, froglights
• Light from torches in your hand (turn on Horizon's Dynamic lights in Extras)
• Waving leaves, grass, flowers and crops
• Water with waves, reflections, refraction and the sun's glint
• A deeper sky with warm sunsets, sun rays, sun glare and haze
• Mobs take the sun's shadow; the Nether and the End get their own light

Every effect can be changed or turned off in the game: Options > Horizon Settings > Shader Packs > Shader Options. The quality is yours to pick there too: turn shadows off for the least GPU time, or choose the shadow map's detail (1024 to 4096) and distance (64 to 160 blocks). The defaults are soft shadows over 96 blocks with water reflections.

Original code, no Minecraft assets. Source: https://github.com/hildlabs/horizon-shaders

shaders.name: Lumina
shaders.summary: High performance with real-time shadows, physical water, roof overhang occlusion, volumetric 3D clouds, and sharp anti-aliasing
shaders.description:
Native shaders designed for high frame rates and clean, balanced visuals without post-processing blur. All options are fully configurable directly in the shader settings menu.

Lighting & Overhang Shading
• Balanced daytime lighting with warm sun and clean azure shadows.
• Directional sky dome occlusion: accurate contrast between ground, walls, and ceilings.
• Non-linear ambient occlusion under house roofs, eaves, porches, and balconies.
• Selective midtone vibrance on grass and foliage without clipping bright highlights.
• Foliage subsurface scattering and sun-facing rim lighting.

Shadows
• Real-time sun and moon shadow maps with distortion-aware filtering.
• Acne-free shadows on terrain, blocks, and thin grass at any distance.
• Selectable shadow map resolution: 512, 1024, 1536, or 2048.

Clarity Anti-Aliasing (FXAA)
• Edge-selective geometric smoothing on block silhouettes, roofs, and stairs.
• Flat surfaces, textures, wood, stone, and UI remain 100% sharp with zero blurring.
• Modes: Sharp, Smooth, or Off.

Water & Underwater
• High-speed Screen Space Reflections (SSR) combined with planar mirror reflections.
• Physics-based Beer-Lambert light absorption with depth-dependent color transition.
• Snell's window when looking up from underwater with total internal reflection.
• Animated seabed caustics, wave refraction, and underwater depth fog.

Clouds & Atmosphere
• Raymarched procedural 3D cumulus clouds with Fast, Balanced, and Cinematic presets.
• Volumetric god rays through terrain and trees.
• Procedural rain puddles on grass and dirt with raindrop impact ripples.
• Custom weather rendering for rain and snow particles.
• Native block emission and dynamic colored lighting support.

Setup Note:
Set Clouds to OFF in your video settings to let the custom 3D clouds render properly.

resourcepacks.name: Menu Panorama
resourcepacks.summary: Put your own wallpaper behind the main menu in Horizon — Minecraft 26.3, rewritten in Rust.
resourcepacks.description:
Menu Panorama is a resource pack for Horizon — Minecraft: Java Edition 26.3, rewritten from scratch in Rust.

It replaces the six textures of the main-menu background with a picture you choose. It is a plain resource pack, not a Java mod: no mod loader, no Java, and no code from the pack is executed. Horizon loads it natively.
• Any photo in the room mode: the picture is shown whole on the four walls, with mirrored seams and soft colours above and below.
• A 360° equirectangular panorama in the 360 mode: the sphere is cut into six cube faces, so the view stays seamless when the camera turns.
• Auto picks the mode from the image's aspect ratio.

Build a pack in the browser with panorama-maker.html: drop an image, choose a face size, download the .zip. Everything runs locally; the picture never leaves the computer. make_panorama.py does the same from the command line.

The pack only changes assets/minecraft/textures/gui/title/background/panorama_0..5.png; gameplay, sounds and other textures are untouched. pack.mcmeta is made for Horizon 26.3 (resource format 97) and also declares formats 15–999, so the same file loads in Minecraft Java 1.21+. A demo pack is attached to every release.

MIT licensed. Source, the browser generator and the CLI are in the repository.
